decisions.rationale: Valid. Origin: this delivery (README line 193 was added in the loop-7 correction b5b542a7; it is not on origin/main 1814ba7d). Reconciler runs on fresh git-archive copies of the lab at b5b542a7 (JDK 25.0.5+8, Maven 3.9.16, mvn -q -o test offline against a private copy of the delivery's local repository; the untouched starter fails exactly the 12 declared failingTests, 10 failures and 2 errors; the private completed solution passes 12/12 with no output): with step 3's controller built on the context's @MockitoBean and the verify kept on the plain mock, the test fails with Mockito's 'Wanted but not invoked'; built on the context mock and verified on the context mock, it fails with the shipped 'step 3: call create on the controller you built, with POSTED'; with the plain-mock verify removed, it fails with 'No interactions wanted here' (first clause of the row, correct); with the full plain-mock step 3 done plus an extra MockMvc request in the test, it fails with 'No interactions wanted here' on the context mock. The critic's MockMvc-instead-of-built variant was not repeated. So the row's second clause is wrong in two ways: 'a controller built with the context's mock' never produces this message, and the MockMvc case produces it only when the call reaches the context mock in addition to, not instead of, the plain mock. Learner impact and delivery decision: low; leaving it as a follow-up does not mislead learners enough to require a fix before delivery. A learner who sees this message has either missed the plain-mock verify (the row's first clause names that correctly) or sent an extra call to the context mock (the row's second clause still points at a call reaching the context's @MockitoBean and at step 3); the wrong example cannot be the learner's situation, because that route fails with other messages that the 'Wanted but not invoked' row and the shipped step 3 message already explain. Nothing sends the learner to a wrong action that a test would then accept. Follow-up for a later module branch: reword the second clause to 'or a call also reached the context's @MockitoBean (for example an extra MockMvc request in this test)' and drop the 'controller built with the context's mock' example. No further correction loop is authorized in this lane after the single loop-7 correction (supervisor decision validation-loop7-o3, done at b5b542a7); fixing this needs a new supervisor decision.

Valid. Origin: this delivery (Task 5, including line 83's 'no @Valid is needed here', was added by this branch; origin/main 1814ba7d README has Tasks 1-4 only). Spring Framework reference (Web on Servlet Stack > Annotated Controllers > Validation, cited with retrieval dates by both critics) states that a class-level @Validated applies method validation through an AOP proxy and must be removed to use Spring MVC's built-in method validation. Reconciler runs on fresh git-archive copies of the lab at b5b542a7 (JDK 25.0.5+8, Maven 3.9.16, mvn -q -o test offline against a private copy of the delivery's local repository; the untouched starter fails exactly the 12 declared failingTests, 10 failures and 2 errors; the private completed solution passes 12/12 with no output): the completed solution with a class-level @Validated added to BookingController and the constraint kept makes task5ReproducesTheZeroIdReport, task5PredictsTheProblemBodyOfTheFix and task5RejectsANonPositiveIdWith400 end in errors: ServletException 'Request processing failed' caused by jakarta.validation.ConstraintViolationException 'byId.id: must be greater than 0'. README and Troubleshooting have no row for this. Learner impact and delivery decision: low; leaving it as a follow-up does not mislead learners enough to require a fix before delivery. The route is plausible (pre-6.1 tutorials required class-level @Validated for path-variable constraints) but nothing in the README, hints or module pages prompts it, the failure is loud and names the constraint violation, the step 3 hint gives the intended placement, and no wrong solution is accepted. Follow-up for a later module branch: add 'and no @Validated on the class' to Task 5 step 3 and a Troubleshooting row for ConstraintViolationException in the Task 5 tests. No further correction loop is authorized in this lane after the single loop-7 correction (supervisor decision validation-loop7-o3, done at b5b542a7); fixing this needs a new supervisor decision.

Valid. Origin: this delivery (README line 196 was added in the loop-7 correction b5b542a7 together with the HandlerMethodValidationException check; not on origin/main). Spring Framework reference (Web on Servlet Stack > Annotated Controllers > Validation, cited with retrieval dates by both critics) states that a class-level @Validated applies method validation through an AOP proxy and must be removed to use Spring MVC's built-in method validation. Reconciler runs on fresh git-archive copies of the lab at b5b542a7 (JDK 25.0.5+8, Maven 3.9.16, mvn -q -o test offline against a private copy of the delivery's local repository; the untouched starter fails exactly the 12 declared failingTests, 10 failures and 2 errors; the private completed solution passes 12/12 with no output): a class-level @Validated alone gives unhandled ConstraintViolationException errors in the three Task 5 tests (no Troubleshooting row, as in cg-education-validation-016); a class-level @Validated plus an ApiErrors handler that turns ConstraintViolationException into a 400 problem fails only task5RejectsANonPositiveIdWith400 with the shipped 'not a check you wrote by hand' message, although no check was written by hand. The test's verdict is right (that is not the Spring MVC built-in method validation the task asks for); only the diagnosis wording is incomplete. Learner impact and delivery decision: low; leaving it as a follow-up does not mislead learners enough to require a fix before delivery. Reaching the message by this route needs two additions nothing in the lab prompts (class-level @Validated and a new ConstraintViolationException handler); the message still names the fix the lab wants (a Bean Validation constraint on the byId parameter answered by Spring's method validation), and the shipped check rejects the route, so no wrong solution passes. Follow-up for a later module branch: extend the row to name class-level @Validated as the other cause. No further correction loop is authorized in this lane after the single loop-7 correction (supervisor decision validation-loop7-o3, done at b5b542a7); fixing this needs a new supervisor decision.

Valid. Origin: mixed. The spot-check command 'mvn -q -o spring-boot:run' (expected/test-summary.txt line 15) and the README Offline note 'No database and no port are used' are main-era (present on origin/main 1814ba7d, line 13 and README line 80). The GET /bookings/0 spot-check lines 21-23 were added by this delivery in an earlier loop and reworded in loop 7 to 'compare them with your Task 5 prediction'. Reconciler run: in a git-archive copy of b5b542a7 with the completed solution, offline against the private copy of the delivery's local repository, mvn -q -o spring-boot:run exits at once with 'No plugin found for prefix 'spring-boot' in the current project and in the plugin groups'; the starter pom declares no spring-boot-maven-plugin and that repository holds none. The reconciler did not re-run the setup command; that go-offline does not fetch an undeclared plugin is inference from the pom. git grep at b5b542a7 finds the same offline spot-check command in six other Spring Boot labs and no Spring Boot lab starter pom declaring the plugin, so the defect is course-wide. Learner impact and delivery decision: low; leaving it as a follow-up does not mislead learners enough to require a fix before delivery. The spot check is optional, fails loudly at once, does not affect the test command or any objective, and the delivery-added prediction comparison has a working primary route in README Task 5 (the .andDo(print()) route into the surefire output file; the reconciler did not re-run that route, the education critic's loop-7 recheck of cg-education-validation-011 did). Follow-up on a course-level or tooling branch for all Spring Boot labs (declare the plugin and prove the offline run, or drop -o and say the spot check needs the network once), and qualify this lab's Offline note for port 8080. No further correction loop is authorized in this lane after the single loop-7 correction (supervisor decision validation-loop7-o3, done at b5b542a7); fixing this needs a new supervisor decision.

Valid as a fact; accepted as a main-era coverage gap and acknowledged residual, not escalated. Origin: mixed. global-error-handling#o1 is claimed in origin/main 1814ba7d lab.json, task2TurnsAnUnknownIdIntoAProblem404 is identical to origin/main, and README Task 2 differs from origin/main only by the '(S9)' day label; README line 123 ('each answer is your ApiErrors problem body', in Task 7) is delivery text. So the 'for all controllers in one @RestControllerAdvice' half has no executing check, and line 123 overstates what the checks confirm under that route. Why not blocking: authoring/docs/lab-contract.md and workflow.md set no rule that each part of a claimed objective needs an executing check, T25 blocks only open critical or high findings, and the gap is in verification, not in learner direction: README Task 2 tells the learner to create ApiErrors as a @RestControllerAdvice class, Troubleshooting row 184 reinforces it, and nothing prompts controller-local handlers, so a learner following the README practises the global form. Learner impact: a learner who deliberately writes local handlers is not told they missed the objective; for a learner following the README, line 123 is true. Leaving line 123 as a follow-up does not mislead learners enough to require a fix before delivery. Per supervisor decision validation-loop7-o3 this delivery does not repair unrelated main-era objectives.
